    Mobile Dog Grooming FAQs

    How much does mobile dog grooming cost in the USA in 2026?

    A full mobile groom typically costs $60–$250 per session in 2026, depending on your dog's size and coat: small dogs (under 25 lb) $60–$90, medium dogs (25–50 lb) $80–$130, large dogs (50–100 lb) $100–$160 or more, and XL dogs (100+ lb) $150–$220 or more. Doodles and other heavy-coated breeds can reach $190–$260 or more. The national average grooming session is $85–$104. All figures are third-party estimates, not quotes.

    Why does mobile grooming cost more than a salon groom?

    Mobile grooming usually carries a 20–30% premium over salon prices because the groomer travels to your home, works one-to-one in a fully equipped van, and your dog skips the crate wait and car ride. You are paying for doorstep convenience and undivided attention, not just the groom itself.

    How much is a bath and brush only, without a haircut?

    A bath and brush only service typically costs $45–$110 in 2026, depending on size and coat. It covers a bath, blow-dry, brush-out and usually a nail check, but no clip or haircut — a good lower-cost option between full grooms.

    How much does it cost to groom a doodle or other heavy-coated breed?

    Doodles and heavy-coated breeds sit at the top of the price range — up to $190–$260 or more for large and XL dogs — because curly, dense coats take longer to wash, dry, brush out and clip, and matting adds extra time. Regular 4–8 week bookings help keep the coat (and the price) under control.

    How often should I book mobile grooming?

    Most groomers rebook every 4–8 weeks. That cycle keeps coats from matting, keeps nails at a healthy length, and is the standard recurring schedule mobile groomers build their routes around.

    How far ahead are mobile groomers booked up?

    In most metro areas, good mobile groomers are booking weeks to months ahead, and some have closed their books to new clients. That is why it pays to request quotes early, be flexible on day and time, and rebook your next visit at each appointment.

    What is included in a full groom?

    A full groom generally includes a bath, blow-dry, brush-out, a haircut or clip to your chosen style, nail trim, and ear cleaning. Teeth cleaning and de-matting are commonly offered as add-ons — confirm exactly what is included when you request your quote, as packages vary by groomer.

    Can a mobile groomer groom my cat too?

    Some mobile groomers accept cats, but many are dog-only because cats need different handling, products and a calm, dog-free van. If you need cat grooming, say so in your quote request and ask specifically — availability varies by groomer and metro.

    Is mobile grooming better for anxious, nervous or senior dogs?

    For many anxious, nervous and senior dogs, yes. There are no other dogs barking, no crate waiting and no car journey — just one groomer, one dog, at home. Senior dogs benefit from a shorter, gentler appointment without standing in a busy salon. Tell the groomer about anxiety, age or health issues in your quote request so they can allow extra time.

    Does this website book a groomer or send my request for me?

    No. This site sends nothing to any groomer. The estimator and quote request pack are free tools that run in your browser: the pack writes a clear, ready-to-send request that you download, copy or email to groomers you choose yourself. A groomer-matching service is a possible future launch model only — it is not operating today.
